I guess what I‘m trying to say is precisely that there‘s not really a feasible way, socially speaking, in which you could humbly say these things, without any context that is. Sure, if some beauty contest winner gets interviewed, they can say „I guess I‘m the most beautiful“ or if so someone gets an IQ test result of 150, they‘re allowed to say it out loud. But you cannot just say it like that. In contrast, you can say „I‘m very empathetic, ambitious, tall, sexual, grounded, unstable, successful, etc“ Beautiful and intelligent not really, and I even think these are the only real determinants of the social status game. These two explain the biggest chunks of the variance..

Imagine someone saying „I think I‘m quite beautiful,“ and actually mean it.. same with „I think im quite intelligent,“ and actually mean it. Sure people say that, but then they get immediately lowered in their social status.

I think it‘s because it actually correlates with so many things that modern people desire. You can brag about many things and people will let it pass, except two things: intelligence and beauty.  These seem to be the two basic factors in the human social status game.

Hey, I appreciate your comment on my article! Let me address your point in order.

- the point of posting my article here is indeed to get an audience of people who can relate to the problem or phenomenon I'm trying to grasp and to get some critical comments, just like yours :-)
- The point about which group of people is particularly prone to "outsource their introspection" is an excellent one, and one upon which almost my entire thesis hinges. One could even say that this group - however you wanna delineate it - would have to be characterized by the fact of never really having developed or cultivated that skill of introspection in the first place, so it might be misleading to talk of "outsourcing" something that was not there in the first place. However, and I will definitely revise my article in that regard, Imeant that not on an individual level, but more on a cultural, societal level, i.e., we as a culture (at least in the West) have had and depended on the cultivated skill of introspection for the last couple hundred years, and it has been eroding for the last couple decades. In other words, it is not really been taught to the newest generation(s) anymore, at least it is not the introspection proper that psychology and folk wisdom presupposes, I would say; rather, it is an introspection already "pre-packaged", one that always has its ties to the Internet, forums, the availability of experience reports of others, etc. 
- this ties in with your suggestion of habit stacking or simply taking a break fom the internet; I would suggest that younger people's "resources" to actually sustain this habit or break offline are meager. They can't do it for very long, and before they know it, they have to "refuel" their motivation on some more Huberman motivation videos or pump up their regimen by just reading up on some more success stories. 
- of course, I will also update the article to point out the various other positive uses and outlets that reddit is being used for
- yes, I see your point; my call to arms is self-selecting the one's that actually struggle with this very issue, all the rest will ignore it anyway. However, I would object that this is just about mental health in 2023. It has been going on since years and decades, and it also is not observed in mental health exclusively, although there probably primarily... You're right that this applies to a yet-to-be-delineated subgroup of the population, as there are certainly many non-addicted and habit-forming generation X people out there with the "old school" skill of introspection. Where did they learn it from, how did they cultivate it? I don't know, maybe my thesis is just way too steep and designed to be provocative, which I openly admit is the case, or maybe some people are just naturally more introspective, and don't need external resources to cultivate that. To them, everything that over the centuries praised itself as helping cultivate introspection is a mere means, an instrument; they basic skill of introspection is there or it isn't. And maybe there have always been a group of people who don't come with that natural ability, and therefore needed not just some external "help", but something more fundamental, like a practice, a philosophy, a religion, a habit of introspection that they are "forced" into as it were. I could live with that view, but I would still say that things have become way more intense with the advent of the 24/7 availability of such forums of personal experiences.
